hints.title: Two-Island Minimum Bridge Obstacle
hints.text: Given exactly two disconnected islands in an N x N grid, finding the minimum count of 0 cells to flip to connect them requires isolating one island completely. How can multi-source expansion bridge the gap?

hints.title: First Island Wavefront Invariant
hints.text: Locate the first island and recolor all its cells to 2 while seeding them into a queue. Expanding outward layer by layer from island 1 until touching island 2 yields the shortest bridge.

hints.title: Two-Phase Island Connection Procedure
hints.text: Step 1: Scan grid to find the first 1 cell. Flood-fill all connected land cells of this first island, setting grid[r][c] = 2 and adding coordinates to queue. Step 2: Level-order wave expansion from queue. For each popped cell, check 4 neighbors. If neighbor is 1, return current distance. If neighbor is 0, set grid[nr][nc] = 2 and enqueue.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: grid width and height (2 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Every cell is visited at most twice (once for coloring island 1, once for expansion).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Measuring all pairs of coordinates between island 1 and island 2 takes O(N^4) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place grid cell marking avoids allocating separate visited structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using depth search to isolate island 1 followed by multi-source breadth-first expansion.

solutions.approach: Two-phase traversal: flood-fill island 1 then multi-source bridge expansion
